absent: Full taskstats record layout beyond the visible interrupt delay tail.
Kernel side handling, locking, and state transitions for taskstats, TCP options, and TEE ioctls.
Wire behavior, retransmission timers, congestion control algorithms, and authentication cryptography.
Memory ownership, lifetime, and error codes for shared memory and zerocopy paths.
Meanings of remaining TEE ioctl commands and parameter combinations beyond the shown range.

findings.text: TASKSTATS_GENL_NAME is TASKSTATS while TASKSTATS_GENL_VERSION is 1, providing the rendezvous point for user requests and kernel events.

TASKSTATS_CMD_UNSPEC reserves 0 while TASKSTATS_CMD_GET follows for user to kernel requests and TASKSTATS_CMD_NEW follows for kernel to user events, with TASKSTATS_CMD_MAX defined as one less than the private sentinel.

TASKSTATS_TYPE_UNSPEC reserves 0 while TASKSTATS_TYPE_PID follows for process identifier and TASKSTATS_TYPE_TGID follows for thread group and TASKSTATS_TYPE_STATS follows for statistics record and TASKSTATS_TYPE_AGGR_PID follows for aggregated pid and TASKSTATS_TYPE_AGGR_TGID follows for aggregated tgid and TASKSTATS_TYPE_NULL follows for empty, with TASKSTATS_TYPE_MAX one less than the sentinel.

TASKSTATS_CMD_ATTR_UNSPEC reserves 0 while TASKSTATS_CMD_ATTR_PID follows for process identifier and TASKSTATS_CMD_ATTR_TGID follows for thread group and TASKSTATS_CMD_ATTR_REGISTER_CPUMASK follows for registration and TASKSTATS_CMD_ATTR_DEREGISTER_CPUMASK follows for deregistration, with TASKSTATS_CMD_ATTR_MAX one less than the sentinel.
The visible tail of the task statistics record carries irq_delay_max_ts of type __kernel_timespec reporting maximum interrupt delay with timespec resolution.

The tcphdr record starts with source with dest plus seq with ack_seq, continues with an endian dependent cluster for doff with res1 and ae with cwr and ece and urg and ack and psh and rst and syn and fin, and ends with window plus check plus urg_ptr.
The control cluster orders data offset with reserved bits and control flags oppositely for little endian versus big endian bitfields, and compilation stops when neither byte order macro is present.
The tcp_word_hdr union overlays hdr with words array of five elements so the header can be read as words, and tcp_flag_word selects the fourth element where offset and flags live.

TCP_FLAG_AE corresponds to byte swapped 0x01000000 while TCP_FLAG_CWR corresponds to byte swapped 0x00800000 while TCP_FLAG_ECE corresponds to byte swapped 0x00400000 while TCP_FLAG_URG corresponds to byte swapped 0x00200000 while TCP_FLAG_ACK corresponds to byte swapped 0x00100000.

TCP_FLAG_PSH corresponds to byte swapped 0x00080000 while TCP_FLAG_RST corresponds to byte swapped 0x00040000 while TCP_FLAG_SYN corresponds to byte swapped 0x00020000 while TCP_FLAG_FIN corresponds to byte swapped 0x00010000, with TCP_RESERVED_BITS masked by byte swapped 0x0E000000 and TCP_DATA_OFFSET masked by byte swapped 0xF0000000.
TCP_MSS_DEFAULT uses 536 for IPv4 operation while TCP_MSS_DESIRED uses 1220 for tunneled IPv6 and EDNS0 style operation.

TCP_NODELAY uses 1 for Nagle control while TCP_MAXSEG uses 2 for MSS limit while TCP_CORK uses 3 for corking while TCP_KEEPIDLE uses 4 for keepalive start while TCP_KEEPINTVL uses 5 for keepalive spacing while TCP_KEEPCNT uses 6 for keepalive count while TCP_SYNCNT uses 7 for SYN retries while TCP_LINGER2 uses 8 for FIN WAIT2 lifetime while TCP_DEFER_ACCEPT uses 9 for data gated wakeup while TCP_WINDOW_CLAMP uses 10 for advertised window bound.

TCP_INFO uses 11 for connection diagnostics while TCP_QUICKACK uses 12 for quick acknowledgement control while TCP_CONGESTION uses 13 for algorithm selection while TCP_MD5SIG uses 14 for RFC2385 signatures, then numbering skips 15 before TCP_THIN_LINEAR_TIMEOUTS uses 16 for thin linear timeouts while TCP_THIN_DUPACK uses 17 for single dupack retransmit while TCP_USER_TIMEOUT uses 18 for loss retry deadline while TCP_REPAIR uses 19 for repair mode.

TCP_REPAIR_QUEUE uses 20 for queue selection while TCP_QUEUE_SEQ uses 21 for queue sequence while TCP_REPAIR_OPTIONS uses 22 for repair options while TCP_FASTOPEN uses 23 for listener Fast Open while TCP_TIMESTAMP uses 24 for timestamp control while TCP_NOTSENT_LOWAT uses 25 for unsent bytes limit while TCP_CC_INFO uses 26 for congestion info while TCP_SAVE_SYN uses 27 for SYN recording while TCP_SAVED_SYN uses 28 for SYN retrieval while TCP_REPAIR_WINDOW uses 29 for window parameters.

TCP_FASTOPEN_CONNECT uses 30 for connect time Fast Open while TCP_ULP uses 31 for upper layer attachment while TCP_MD5SIG_EXT uses 32 for extended signatures while TCP_FASTOPEN_KEY uses 33 for cookie key while TCP_FASTOPEN_NO_COOKIE uses 34 for cookieless Fast Open while TCP_ZEROCOPY_RECEIVE uses 35 for zerocopy receive while TCP_INQ uses 36 for queue occupancy notifications, with TCP_CM_INQ defined as an alias of the same value.

TCP_TX_DELAY uses 37 for transmit delay in microseconds while TCP_AO_ADD_KEY uses 38 for key install while TCP_AO_DEL_KEY uses 39 for key removal while TCP_AO_INFO uses 40 for per socket authentication options while TCP_AO_GET_KEYS uses 41 for key listing while TCP_AO_REPAIR uses 42 for sequence repair, and TCP_IS_MPTCP uses 43 for multipath query while TCP_RTO_MAX_MS uses 44 for maximum retransmit timeout while TCP_RTO_MIN_US uses 45 for minimum timeout while TCP_DELACK_MAX_US uses 46 for delayed acknowledgement limit, with repair enable 1 and disable 0 and disable without probes negative 1.

The tcp_repair_opt record pairs opt_code with opt_val while the tcp_repair_window record groups snd_wl1 with snd_wnd and max_window and rcv_wnd and rcv_wup, plus TCP_NO_QUEUE starts the selector and TCP_RECV_QUEUE follows for receive and TCP_SEND_QUEUE follows for send before TCP_QUEUES_NR counts them.

TFO_STATUS_UNSPEC starts as catch all while TFO_COOKIE_UNAVAILABLE indicates missing cookie outside cookieless mode while TFO_DATA_NOT_ACKED indicates SYN data not acknowledged while TFO_SYN_RETRANSMITTED indicates SYN retransmission after timeout, in that order.

TCPI_OPT_TIMESTAMPS uses 1 for timestamps while TCPI_OPT_SACK uses 2 for selective acknowledgement while TCPI_OPT_WSCALE uses 4 for window scaling while TCPI_OPT_ECN uses 8 for negotiated ECN while TCPI_OPT_ECN_SEEN uses 16 for observed marks while TCPI_OPT_SYN_DATA uses 32 for SYN data acknowledgement while TCPI_OPT_USEC_TS uses 64 for microsecond timestamps while TCPI_OPT_TFO_CHILD uses 128 for Fast Open child.

TCP_CA_Open uses 0 for healthy operation while TCP_CA_Disorder uses 1 for duplicate driven suspicion while TCP_CA_CWR uses 2 for ECN driven reduction while TCP_CA_Recovery uses 3 for acknowledgement driven retransmission while TCP_CA_Loss uses 4 for timeout driven recovery, with TCPF_CA_Open and companions providing one hot bit wrappers.

TCPI_ECN_MODE_DISABLED uses 0 for disabled while TCPI_ECN_MODE_RFC3168 uses 1 for classic negotiation while TCPI_ECN_MODE_ACCECN uses 2 for accurate reporting while TCPI_ECN_MODE_PENDING uses 3 for pending, while TCP_ACCECN_OPT_NOT_SEEN uses 0 for unseen and TCP_ACCECN_OPT_EMPTY_SEEN uses 1 for empty and TCP_ACCECN_OPT_COUNTER_SEEN uses 2 for counter and TCP_ACCECN_OPT_FAIL_SEEN uses 3 for failure, with TCP_ACCECN_ACE_FAIL_SEND and TCP_ACCECN_ACE_FAIL_RECV and TCP_ACCECN_OPT_FAIL_SEND and TCP_ACCECN_OPT_FAIL_RECV occupying bits 0 through 3 for send versus receive failure detail.

The connection diagnostics record opens with single byte state and congestion state and retransmit and probe and backoff and option fields, then packs send and receive window scales as nibbles plus application limited and Fast Open failure bits, followed by round trip and acknowledgement timers and segment sizes and unacknowledged and selective acknowledgement and loss and retransmit counters with last data and acknowledgement timestamps.

The diagnostics record continues with path and congestion metrics and receive side round trip and space, lifetime retransmission totals, pacing and delivery rates, acknowledged and received byte and segment totals, unsent bytes and minimum round trip with data segment counts, delivery rate, busy and window limited and buffer limited microsecond times, delivered totals with ECN marked subset, sent and retransmitted bytes with duplicate and reordering and out of order counts, scaled send and receive windows, rehash count, RTO totals and recovery time, ECN byte detail, and a final packed field for ECN mode plus ACC ECN visibility plus failure mode.

TCP_NLA_PAD starts the sequence while TCP_NLA_BUSY follows for busy time while TCP_NLA_RWND_LIMITED follows for window limited time while TCP_NLA_SNDBUF_LIMITED follows for buffer limited time while TCP_NLA_DATA_SEGS_OUT follows for data segments out while TCP_NLA_TOTAL_RETRANS follows for retransmit total while TCP_NLA_PACING_RATE follows for pacing rate while TCP_NLA_DELIVERY_RATE follows for delivery rate while TCP_NLA_SND_CWND follows for congestion window while TCP_NLA_REORDERING follows for reordering while TCP_NLA_MIN_RTT follows for minimum RTT while TCP_NLA_RECUR_RETRANS follows for recurring retransmits while TCP_NLA_DELIVERY_RATE_APP_LMT follows for application limit flag while TCP_NLA_SNDQ_SIZE follows for send queue size while TCP_NLA_CA_STATE follows for congestion state.

TCP_NLA_SND_SSTHRESH continues for slow start threshold while TCP_NLA_DELIVERED continues for delivered total while TCP_NLA_DELIVERED_CE continues for ECN marked delivered while TCP_NLA_BYTES_SENT continues for bytes sent while TCP_NLA_BYTES_RETRANS continues for bytes retransmitted while TCP_NLA_DSACK_DUPS continues for duplicate reports while TCP_NLA_REORD_SEEN continues for reordering sightings while TCP_NLA_SRTT continues for smoothed RTT while TCP_NLA_TIMEOUT_REHASH continues for timeout rehash while TCP_NLA_BYTES_NOTSENT continues for unsent bytes while TCP_NLA_EDT continues for departure time while TCP_NLA_TTL continues for hop limit while TCP_NLA_REHASH continues for combined rehash, all increasing sequentially from the earlier group.

MD5 signature support caps keys at 80 bytes, defines extension flags for address prefix length and interface index, stores a peer address with flags and prefix length and key length and device index and binary key, and provides a diagnostics variant holding family and prefix and key length with a four word address and key.

Authentication option keys cap at 80 bytes with flags for virtual routing interface and for excluding other options from authentication, where the install record carries peer address and algorithm name and device index and current versus next key selectors and address prefix with send and receive identifiers and authentication length and key material, while the removal record carries peer address and device index and selectors including asynchronous list handling with current and next identifiers.

Authentication option management adds an info record with current and next selectors and required mode and counter control and ICMP acceptance plus packet outcome counters, a query record that filters by peer and identifiers and current or next or all selection and returns algorithm and key with verification counts, and a repair record holding initial sequence numbers with send and receive sequence number extensions, all aligned to eight bytes with reserved fields zero.

Zerocopy receive defines a TLB clean hint flag of 1 and an exchange record carrying mapping address with length and skip hint and queue occupancy and socket error, plus copy buffer address with length, flags, ancillary data pointer with length, message flags, and a reserved zero field.

TEE_IOC_MAGIC uses 0xA4 while TEE_IOC_BASE uses 0 while TEE_MAX_ARG_SIZE uses 4096, with TEE_GEN_CAP_GP in bit 0 for GlobalPlatform compliance and TEE_GEN_CAP_PRIVILEGED in bit 1 for supplicant use and TEE_GEN_CAP_REG_MEM in bit 2 for shared memory registration and TEE_GEN_CAP_MEMREF_NULL in bit 3 for null memory reference and TEE_GEN_CAP_OBJREF in bit 4 for object reference, plus TEE_MEMREF_NULL and TEE_OBJREF_NULL as all ones 64 bit sentinels.
TEE_IMPL_ID_OPTEE uses 1 while TEE_IMPL_ID_AMDTEE uses 2 while TEE_IMPL_ID_TSTEE uses 3 while TEE_IMPL_ID_QTEE uses 4, with TEE_OPTEE_CAP_TZ marking TrustZone support in bit 0.
tee_ioctl_version_data groups impl_id with impl_caps and gen_caps while tee_ioctl_shm_alloc_data groups size with flags and id while tee_ioctl_buf_data pairs buf_ptr with buf_len.
TEE_IOC_VERSION reads tee_ioctl_version_data at base plus zero while TEE_IOC_SHM_ALLOC exchanges tee_ioctl_shm_alloc_data at base plus one, both keyed by TEE_IOC_MAGIC.

TEE_IOCTL_PARAM_ATTR_TYPE_NONE uses 0 for unused while TEE_IOCTL_PARAM_ATTR_TYPE_VALUE_INPUT uses 1 for value input and TEE_IOCTL_PARAM_ATTR_TYPE_VALUE_OUTPUT uses 2 for value output and TEE_IOCTL_PARAM_ATTR_TYPE_VALUE_INOUT uses 3 for bidirectional value, skipping 4 before TEE_IOCTL_PARAM_ATTR_TYPE_MEMREF_INPUT uses 5 and TEE_IOCTL_PARAM_ATTR_TYPE_MEMREF_OUTPUT uses 6 and TEE_IOCTL_PARAM_ATTR_TYPE_MEMREF_INOUT uses 7, with TEE_IOCTL_PARAM_ATTR_TYPE_UBUF_INPUT at 8 and TEE_IOCTL_PARAM_ATTR_TYPE_UBUF_OUTPUT at 9 and TEE_IOCTL_PARAM_ATTR_TYPE_UBUF_INOUT at 10 and TEE_IOCTL_PARAM_ATTR_TYPE_OBJREF_INPUT at 11 and TEE_IOCTL_PARAM_ATTR_TYPE_OBJREF_OUTPUT at 12 and TEE_IOCTL_PARAM_ATTR_TYPE_OBJREF_INOUT at 13, selected by TEE_IOCTL_PARAM_ATTR_TYPE_MASK of 0xFF.

Several records require reserved and padding fields to stay zero with eight byte alignment for authentication structures, MD5 and AO keys are bounded by 80 bytes, and last acknowledgement sent time is explicitly not retained.
Both TCP and TEE user headers define include guards _UAPI_LINUX_TCP_H and __TEE_H that prevent multiple inclusion.
